title: State Pages, Owner Auto Policy — Reinstatement Fee Basis Under the Company's State Schedule
content:
**Rule.** For a reinstatement with lapse of an Owner Auto Policy term, the company's state schedule sets the basis of the reinstatement fee by the term's garaging state. The basis is the figure the reinstatement fee starts from.

| Garaging state | Reinstatement fee basis |
|---|---|
| Florida, Georgia | 15 percent of the re-written premium booked with the reinstatement (the amount to the cent) |
| Arizona, Texas, Virginia | the greater of the package's reinstatement fee and 30.00 |
| Any other state (for example Ohio) | the package's reinstatement fee |

The fee is rounded once, at the end, to the nearest cent, half up.

**Points of judgement.**
- In Florida and Georgia the basis moves with the re-written premium. A reinstatement whose re-written premium is 0.00 has a basis of 0.00.
- In Arizona, Texas and Virginia the basis is never below 30.00. It is the package's reinstatement fee only where that fee is higher than 30.00.
- The package's reinstatement fee is the figure in the fee schedule.

**Hypothetical illustrations.**
- A Georgia-garaged term with a re-written premium of 412.60 has a basis of 15 percent of 412.60, which is 61.89.
- A Texas-garaged term with a package reinstatement fee of 25.00 has a basis of 30.00.
- An Ohio-garaged term with the same package fee has a basis of 25.00.
